newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares inch up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares inch up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed minimally higher on Tuesday due in part to speculative buying in a group of low-priced issues, brokers said.

The B share index edged up 0.10 points, or 0.12 percent, to end at 89.89 on turnover of HK$11.40 million, compared with Monday's HK$79.00 million. Without major market-moving incentives, the index will move in a tight range for some time, brokers said.
Institutional trade on Tuesday remained focused on several large-cap counters with strong earnings record, they said.
Shenzhen Textile was the session's star on speculative buying, brokers said. The counter rose HK$0.09, or 5.36 percent, to HK$1.77 on trade of 5,500 shares.
Conglomerate Lionda climbed HK$0.09, or 4.27 percent, to HK$2.20 on volume of 13,000 shares.
Guangdong Power, aided by institutional buying, rallied HK$0.06 to HK$5.36, with 397,800 shares traded.
Gujing Distillery put on HK$0.05 to HK$5.45 as volume reached 274,800 shares. Refrigerator maker Meilin closed unchanged at HK$3.17 after 315,400 shares changed hands.
Dadonghai registered the heaviest trade of 1.62 million shares to end off HK$0.01 at HK$1.36 on profit-taking, brokers said.
Automobile parts maker Weifu, the biggest loser, fell HK$0.24, or 7.06 percent, to HK$3.16 on thin volume of 13,000 shares.

The A share market maintained its upward momentum on Tuesday, rising 7.74 points, or 2.36 percent, to close at 335.73. Turnover was 12.25 billion yuan compared with 13.22 billion yuan the previous session. Brokers said that despite the rise, heavy profit-taking looms.
The composite index finished up 6.86 points, or 2.23 percent, at 313.67.

Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd, which listed 30 million A shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ended the session at 10.70 yuan against its recent offer price of 3.50 yuan per share. Volume hit 26.63 million shares.
Large-cap issues traded the most on volume of 100.33 million shares, rising 0.40 yuan to 7.58 yuan.
Universe, which skyrocketed more than 30 percent on Monday, plunged 1.20 yuan, or 13.99 percent, to 7.38 yuan Tuesday.
The real estate developer on Tuesday denied rumours that it had sold a Shenzhen property project to a Hong Kong-based firm.
